texts.preamble: Nadeem Pasha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 14 February, 2025 Scch-21 1 Mvc No.1288/2024 Kabc0B0004192024 In The Court Of Xvii Addl. Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21) Present : Vijaykumar S. Hiremath., L.Lb., Xvii Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru. Dated this the 14th Day of February-2025 M.V.C. No.1288/2024 Petitioner/s: 1. Nadeem Pasha S/o Shek Guljar, Aged about 26 years, R/at No.156A/3, Muslim Mohalla, Sulibele, Bengaluru Rural-562129. (By Sri. B. Y. Ravi, Adv.,) Vs . Respondent/s: 1. United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Motor Claims Hub, 5th & 6th Floor, Krushi Bhavana, Hudson Circle, Nrupatunga road, Bengaluru-560001. (In Policy No.0731013123P111425535 Valid from 09.12.2023 to 08.12.2024) (By Sri. K. Chandra Shekhar, Adv.,) 2. Mr. Bhargava. G S/o G. Ganesh Kumar, R/at No.38, Anikethana, Kuvempunagar Extension, Dasarahalli, Doddurkarpanahalli, Bangarpet, Kolar - 563162. Scch-21 2 Mvc No.1288/2024 (R.C. Owner of the Car bearing Reg. No. Ka-02-Mg-5410) (By Sri. N. S. Sheshadri., Adv.) Date of institution of the : 16.02.2024 Nadeem Pasha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 14 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136766881/ 1 petition Nature of the Petition : U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act Date of commencement of : 29.08.2024 recording of the evidence Date on which the Judgment : 14.02.2025 was pronounced Duration of the Petition Year/s Month/s Day/s 00 11 29 Judgment
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 26.01.2024. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 26.01.2024 at about 06.00 p.m., petitioner was driving the Auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AH-4178, along with passenger near HP Petrol Bunk, OM Road, K. R. Puram, Bengaluru slowly cautiously and observing all traffic rules and regulations, at that time all of a sudden a Car bearing Reg. No. KA-02-MG-5410 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner's auto-rickshaw from behind. Due to impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained several injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, K. R. Puram, Bengaluru, wherein first aid treatment was given and thereafter shifted to MVJ Medical College & Research Hospital, Hoskote, wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 26 years, the petitioner was working as a Driver and earning Rs.40,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income. Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, both the respondents appeared before this court and filed their respective written statements. The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending Car. Nadeem Pasha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 14 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136766881/ 2 Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was in-force as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further it is contended that, as per the discharge summary of the MVJ Hospital, petitioner's auto toppled and not hit by Car, so it is a false case, there is actionable negligence on the part of the petitioner at the time of the accident. Further this respondent No.1 submits that, the petitioner was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident. The respondent No.2 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and submitted that, the accident is occurred on the negligence of the petitioner. Further, both the respondents denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.13 and examined Dr. Nagaraj B. N as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.14 and 15 and also examined MRD In-charge at MVJ Medical College and Hospital as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.16 to Ex.P.18 and closed their side. On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of the respondents.
texts.arguments: In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 16. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,456/- towards medical expenses. Hence, at least 1 month is required to recover from the accidental injuries. It is the further contended that, the injured Nadeem Pasha vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 14 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136766881/ 5 petitioner was a driver and earning Rs.40,000/- per month, in support of his income he has not produced any single document before this court. Thus, there is no cogent material on record to show actual income of the petitioner at the time of accident in question. Hence, income of petitioner is to be fixed notionally. Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.16,500/- under this head. 21. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability- The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. Nagaraj B. N in order to substantiate the same, PW.2 who has deposed that, petitioner has sustained left clavicle fracture and opined that, total physical disability of the left arm at 30% and that of whole body disability at 10%. Admittedly, PW.2 is not a treated doctor. Learned counsel for petitioner argued that, petitioner sustained left Clavicle fracture and he has taken treatment for the same. Further he argued that, due to the said injury petitioner is unable to drive his auto-rickshaw. Hence, requested to consider 10% disability. In support of his argument he relied upon the Judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No. 1556/2016 between Ramachandra Vs. Girija. K and another. But in the said Judgment also the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka observed that, the Clavicle bone is an ornamental bone, the fracture of Clavicle bone does not amount to any disability. Learned Counsel for insurance company argued that, the clavicle bone is only an ornamental bone and the said fracture does not lead to any disability. In support of his argument he relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No. 1602/2016 between Jayanath Kumbar Vs M J Mahesha and another, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, clavicle bone is only an ornamental bone and the fracture does not lead to any disability. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
